speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are experiencing increasing pain and swelling in your right knee, along with episodes of pain during urination. You also mentioned a history of a painful, swollen left ankle that resolved on its own. To understand the pattern of these episodes, can you tell me your age and gender?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis (formerly Reiter's syndrome)

The combination of asymmetric oligoarthritis (knee, then ankle), urethritis (pain with urination), and your history of sexual activity with multiple partners strongly suggests Reactive Arthritis. Given your age, gender, and symptoms, I am requesting a Urinalysis and a HLA-B27 genetic test to confirm this diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, HLA-B27
